title: Degree-choosability of proper conflict-free list coloring of sparse graphs
summary: Given a graph $G$ and a mapping $f:V(G) \to \mathbb{N}$, an $f$-list assignment of $G$ is a function that maps each $v \in V(G)$ to a set of at least $f(v)$ colors. For an $f$-list assignment $L$ of a graph $G$, a proper conflict-free $L$-coloring of $G$ is a proper coloring $φ$ of $G$ such that for every vertex $v \in V(G)$, $φ(v) \in L(v)$ and some appears precisely once in the neighborhood of $v$.
